conclusion: Run 1 of 2 (arms base / stream / streamfile, 5 rounds x 10, alternating order by round; 0 errors; 1,800 of 1,800 answers bit-identical to P1's reference). Cold: stream cuts first-request time by 4.97 s pooled within CPU part (35.91 -> 31.44 s p50, -14 %; CPU part 0xd0c -9.4 s, -19 %); download+load 33.72 -> 29.19 s p50; the download itself is unchanged (24.99 vs 24.99 s), the loader spends 18.7 s of it blocked on bytes. streamfile (llama.cpp's own order) cuts only 1.10 s: the order is what makes the overlap pay. Restore: SnapStart already hides the download and load (both run in publish_version's snapshot init, never in a restore), and stream makes restore WORSE: +0.41 s first-request (3.96 -> 4.35 s p50, +10 %; per-round medians do not overlap) because it uses +470 MB (Max Memory Used 5,160 -> 5,631 MB p50) on cold, restore and warm alike, and the larger snapshot takes longer to restore. Local diagnosis (same zip, real S3, malloc_stats): the extra is glibc thread-arena retention, about 16.7 MiB in each of the 32 download threads' arenas, because the overlapped KleidiAI repack frees large blocks while the download still allocates 8 MiB bodies, raising glibc's dynamic mmap threshold; malloc_trim returns only ~90 MB of it. Run 2 pins the threshold (mallopt M_MMAP_THRESHOLD = 4 MiB; locally: stream peak RSS 4.94 GB vs base 5.00 GB, answers identical) and measures the pin alone on base. Host variability (host_variability; no rerun): recorded cpuinfo CPU part per request (0xd40/0xd0c/0xd4f), the ggml CPU variants (one set per part) and os.cpu_count()=6 per cold environment, and one Lambda runtime (python:3.12.mainlinev2.v43); not recorded, so unknown: cpuinfo implementer/variant, feature flags, HWCAPs, cgroup limits, kernel, AZ and physical host. No Graviton generation is claimed. Every comparison is within one CPU part with arms run sequentially in alternating order each round, and every round's within-part delta has the same sign for each conclusion (stream cold 0xd40 -4.26 to -4.73 s over 5 rounds; stream restore 0xd40 +0.33 to +0.61 s, memory +455 to +505 MB in every round). Limits: no restore landed on 0xd4f; 0xd0c and 0xd4f rest on 2-3 rounds.

hypothesis: On a cold start the baseline downloads the 1,981 MiB Q8_0 GGUF into a memfd (25.0 s p50) and only then lets llama.cpp load it (model_load_mmap 8.4 s p50, which includes KleidiAI repacking each Q8_0 matmul weight as it reads it). The loader reads the header first and then each tensor once, so the load can start as soon as the header is present and repack each tensor as its bytes land. Overlapping the two should cut cold download+load from ~33.4 s towards max(download, load) plus the tail of the last tensors, and change no output. It cannot change a SnapStart restore, which never downloads or loads.

snapstart_note: Under SnapStart the download and load run inside publish_version's snapshot init, never in a restore. The streamed load can only change restore through what the snapshot holds (the same model in the same memory), so restore is the control class: any restore delta beyond run-to-run spread would be a defect or noise. The snapshot init itself (phases.<arm>.restore.snapshot_init) does show the overlap, and it bounds how long publish_version takes, not any request latency.
